purpose: Calibration of the black-box teardown method. Every statement below was written from public black-box material only (website, docs/llms-full.txt, public SPA bundles, DNS, certificate transparency, AWS published IP ranges, status page, job posts) BEFORE any comparison with Bolna's open-source code. A later verifier scores each statement against the code. The hit rate on the 'checkable_in_oss' rows says how far to trust the same inference methods on closed vendors.
not_opened: research/2026-10-17/lanes/l4a-competitors/data/bolna-github-issues.tsv and complaints.csv Bolna GitHub rows (read only AFTER this file was frozen)
research/2026-10-17/lanes/l4a-competitors/report.md, CORRECTIONS-round2.md, ledger.md (read only AFTER this file was frozen)

contamination_incident.what: The lane brief told us to start from l4a parity.csv rows for Bolna. Four of those rows quote the open-source code: voicemail_amd ('LLM classification of transcript every 7 s up to 30 s (OSS voicemail_handler.py)'), dtmf ('dtmf_enabled flag in OSS ConversationConfig'), code_switching ('LLM matrix-language prompt (OSS prompts.py)'), memory_across_calls ('memory/ has only an in-memory scalar cache'). These were seen at 2026-10-20 ~16:00Z before any black-box work.
contamination_incident.handling: Statements touching those four topics carry contamination='yes' and must be EXCLUDED from the calibration hit rate even where we also found independent black-box evidence. Statements near them carry contamination='possible'.
contamination_incident.method_finding: The teardown brief's own 'start from what exists' inputs leak code knowledge into a blind lane. Future blind lanes need a pre-filtered input pack.

confidence_scale: 0-1 = our probability the statement is true of the production system / the OSS code as stated. 'checkable_in_oss' marks whether the open-source repository can confirm or refute it (some claims are about the hosted service only).

inferences.statement: The call pipeline is Bolna's own Python asyncio framework, not Pipecat, LiveKit Agents or Vocode; no dependency on any of these three is present in the open-source core.
evidence: data/teardown/bolna/web/www.bolna.ai_docs_llms-full.txt (0 hits for pipecat/livekit/vocode across 1.9 MB of docs)
docs on-prem guide: images api_server, ws_server, telephone_server, q_manager, q_worker, arq_worker; 'command: arq arq_worker.WorkerSettings' (llms-full.txt lines ~18090-18150)

inferences.statement: An agent is a list of tasks; each task has task_type ('conversation'), a toolchain {execution: 'sequential'|'parallel', pipelines: [[transcriber, llm, synthesizer]]}, tools_config {input, output, transcriber, llm_agent, synthesizer, api_tools} and task_config. The OSS code contains config models with these names and a task manager that walks the pipelines.
evidence: platform bundle default agent object (studio chunk in data/teardown/bolna/platform-scripts/files) with execution:'parallel'

inferences.statement: Each live call is one websocket session on a ws server: the telephony provider's media stream (Twilio/Plivo/Exotel/Vobiz) connects to a ws route keyed by agent_id (plus a run/call id), and the handler runs the transcriber, LLM and synthesizer as concurrent asyncio tasks connected by queues.

A separate telephone server places outbound calls through the provider REST API and answers the provider's call webhook with provider markup (TwiML/Plivo XML) that streams media to the ws server; inbound calls hit the same server first.

Outbound scheduling/queueing (concurrency caps per provider, batches, 10-minute schedule rounding, reschedule outside calling hours) runs in q_manager/q_worker over RabbitMQ with Redis, and this layer is NOT in the open-source repo (OSS has the conversation engine, the hosted platform adds API, scheduling, billing, campaigns, workflows, compliance).
evidence: on-prem prerequisites: Postgres 16, Redis, RabbitMQ mq.m5.large, S3 (llms-full.txt ~18070)
AGENTS.md: scheduled_at rounds up to next 10-minute mark

inferences.statement: LLM calls go through LiteLLM (model strings like 'azure/gpt-4.1-mini', ten extra providers 'routed through LiteLLM'), with OpenAI-compatible custom endpoints via base_url; the OSS core declares litellm as a dependency.
evidence: llms-full.txt ~3702 'Ten more are accepted and routed through LiteLLM'
bundle default llm_config provider:'azure', model:'azure/gpt-4.1-mini', family:'openai'

inferences.statement: Transcribers and synthesizers are one class per provider behind a common base (transcriber: deepgram, azure, sarvam, elevenlabs, assemblyai, gladia, soniox, smallest, openai, gemini; synthesizer: elevenlabs, cartesia, azuretts, polly, deepgram, sarvam, smallest, rime, kalpa, maya, soniox, openai/custom). The OSS repo contains at least deepgram, azure, elevenlabs, cartesia, polly and sarvam classes.
evidence: llms-full.txt synthesizer language Warning listing provider keys (~3773)

inferences.statement: Telephony handlers exist for twilio (mulaw 8 kHz media streams), plivo, exotel and vobiz (linear16 'wav'), sip-trunk (Asterisk, ulaw), trunk (new SIP edge, linear16) and freeswitch (web calls, linear16 16 kHz in / 24 kHz out); 'default' is a plain websocket client used by the playground/chat. OSS contains twilio, plivo and exotel handlers; vobiz/trunk/freeswitch may be closed.

There is no dedicated semantic end-of-turn model (no smart-turn / turn-detector model); end of turn comes from the STT provider's endpointing (Deepgram endpointing ms) or provider-native turn detection (Deepgram Flux, AssemblyAI, Soniox), followed by a configurable linear/incremental delay before the LLM is called.
evidence: Engine tab docs: Endpointing slider only for Deepgram-non-Flux/ElevenLabs/Gladia/OpenAI/Gemini; others detect end of turn themselves (llms-full.txt ~1310-1322)

inferences.statement: Barge-in is transcript-driven: the agent stops speaking once the caller's interim transcript reaches N words (default 2), with a stopword list ('stop', 'wait', 'hold on') that interrupts immediately; there is no acoustic-VAD barge-in in the core.
No local VAD model (e.g. Silero) runs in the main audio path; VAD comes from the STT provider.
evidence: AssemblyAI vad_threshold is a provider setting (llms-full.txt ~6913)

inferences.statement: Hangup is decided by an extra LLM call over the transcript with a 'determine if the conversation is complete' prompt (hangup_after_LLMCall), separate from the conversational LLM.
evidence: bundle string 'You are an AI assistant determining if a conversation is complete' next to the default agent object (platform-scripts/files studio chunk)

inferences.statement: Voicemail detection is an LLM classification of early transcript text, not acoustic AMD.
inferences.contamination: yes (parity.csv voicemail_amd row quotes OSS voicemail_handler.py) - EXCLUDE from hit rate
evidence: bundle: 'voicemail_check' categorised as an llm event (platform-chunks)

inferences.statement: Mid-call language switching uses an LLM language-detection step and then swaps to the per-language STT/TTS set in multilingual_config.
inferences.contamination: yes (parity.csv code_switching row quotes OSS prompts.py) - EXCLUDE

inferences.statement: Ambient background noise is mixed into the agent's outbound audio from bundled audio tracks (default 'office-ambience').

Backchanneling plays short pre-generated acknowledgement clips while the caller is speaking long turns (start delay 5 s, gap 5 s); fillers ('use_fillers') are pre-generated audio played while the LLM is thinking.
Synthesized audio is cached for repeated text (synthesizer.caching:true), so welcome and fixed messages are not re-synthesized on every call.
inferences.contamination: possible (parity memory row mentions an in-memory cache)

inferences.statement: There is no persistent cross-call memory; personalisation is per-call variable injection (user_data, context_data, inbound caller lookup via ingest_source_config from API/CSV/Sheet).
inferences.contamination: yes (parity.csv memory_across_calls row quotes OSS memory/) - EXCLUDE
evidence: llms-full.txt: 0 hits 'cross-call', memory only in vLLM/UI contexts

inferences.statement: DTMF capture is a per-task boolean (dtmf_enabled) in task_config.

The current web call (dashboard test call and Web Call SDK v2) is SIP over WebSocket with SIP.js 0.21.x to FreeSWITCH (fs.bolna.ai), WebRTC Opus with Google STUN; the backend mints a single-use session (wss_url, sip_username/password, ice_servers) at /web-call/freeswitch-session and sends X-Agent-Id / X-Run-Id SIP headers. FreeSWITCH forks call audio to the agent ws pipeline as linear16. No LiveKit/Daily/Twilio Voice SDK.
evidence: llms-full.txt ~3790 'freeswitch, used for web calling (linear16, 16 kHz in / 24 kHz out)'
CT log fs.bolna.ai / fs-dev / fs-staging; DNS fs.bolna.ai 65.2.23.64 ap-south-1

inferences.statement: The FreeSWITCH-to-pipeline bridge is a websocket audio fork (mod_audio_fork / mod_audio_stream style), so a web call enters the same ws pipeline as a phone call with provider 'freeswitch'.
evidence: input/output enum includes 'freeswitch' alongside telephony providers (llms-full.txt ~3790)

inferences.statement: Legacy SIP trunks run on an Asterisk PJSIP media server (sip.bolna.ai, single EC2 IP in ap-south-1) that bridges to the agent with ulaw audio.
evidence: llms-full.txt ~34580 'Asterisk-based SIP media server with the PJSIP channel driver'; ~32745 'ulaw to match Asterisk'

inferences.statement: The new SIP-trunk edge (trunk.bolna.ai, launched 2026-10-15) is a different stack from the legacy Asterisk: FreeSWITCH-based (same team stood up fs.* hosts in Sept 2026), UDP/TCP only, PCMU/PCMA, RTP 30000-40000, refuses delayed-offer INVITEs with 488, IP-ACL gate with 403.
evidence: llms-full.txt ~26153-26175 migration table; AGENTS.md SIP trunks section

inferences.statement: Production runs on AWS. Control plane and India call processing are in ap-south-1 (api.bolna.ai, ws.bolna.ai, ts.bolna.ai each behind an ALB named bolna-*-prod-ingress-alb); a separate US websocket cluster runs in us-east-1 (us.ws.bolna.ai ALB, ws.bolna.dev). The '-ingress-alb' naming indicates Kubernetes (EKS with the AWS Load Balancer Controller).
Bolna runs separate named stacks ('apollo', 'ares', 'topaz') each with api/ws/ts hosts, mostly in ap-south-1 with a US ws for topaz: dedicated cells for large customers or release rings.

Bolna is standing up self-hosted model inference in Mumbai (inference-mumbai.bolna.ai wildcard cert 2026-10-05, no public A record) and has had a self-hosted Deepgram endpoint (deepgram.bolna.ai cert 2025-11-09).

The India-resident path is a restricted deployment: it accepts only Plivo telephony, Azure OpenAI LLM and Bolna-owned provider keys; any BYOK key silently routes the call to the US cluster, so BYOK credential handling exists only in the US stack.

SaaS layer: Vite/React SPA on Vercel (platform.bolna.ai), Next.js marketing site on Vercel, Supabase Auth (auth.bolna.ai CNAME to a supabase.co project) with GitHub/Google OAuth and hCaptcha, Stripe payments, PostHog (managed reverse proxy pthg.bolna.ai) for analytics and feature flags, Sentry, Intercom/Plain support chat, Better Stack status, customer.io email, Metabase Cloud BI, self-hosted Grafana, Mintlify docs.
evidence: data/teardown/bolna/platform-scripts/manifest.json + files (supabase-js, gotrue, 'Secured by Stripe', posthog, sentry, intercom, cdn-plain)
dns doh2-2026-10-20.txt (auth.bolna.ai, pthg, metabase, comms, status)

inferences.statement: Knowledge bases: PDFs parsed with Unsiloed (LlamaParse fallback), embedded with all-mpnet-base-v2, stored in LanceDB (rag_config.vector_store.provider default 'lancedb'), ONNX reranker; retrieval is a tool/step inside the LLM agent.

LLM agent types include 'simple_llm_agent' (single prompt, agent_flow_type 'streaming') and a graph agent (nodes with LLM/expression/event edges, router and static nodes, per-node tools); the graph agent is in the OSS core.

Workflows (multi-step outreach sequences, WhatsApp via AiSensy, node callbacks, workflow campaigns) are a separate closed service (workflows.bolna.ai resolves to private 172.32.x addresses; /rpc/workflows API) and are not in the OSS repo.

Post-call processing (transcript assembly, cost calculation, LLM extractions with confidence and reasoning, recording URL) runs asynchronously after 'call-disconnected' and before 'completed'; webhooks and HTTP tool calls egress from three fixed NAT IPs in ap-south-1 with no HMAC signature.

Call quality is graded internally by LLM-as-judge plus quantitative signal detectors (barge-in, agent interruption) verified by human annotators in Label Studio (annotate.bolna.ai); this pipeline is internal, not a customer-facing optimisation loop.

A new dashboard agent defaults to Vobiz telephony, Deepgram nova-3 'hi' STT (16 kHz linear16, 200 ms endpointing), Azure OpenAI gpt-4.1-mini (max_tokens 250, temperature 0.2), ElevenLabs eleven_turbo_v2_5 voice 'Tripti', ambient 'office-ambience', call_terminate 300 s, hangup_after_silence 15 s, 'are you still there' after 10 s.
evidence: default agent object in the studio bundle (platform-scripts/files, observed 2026-10-20)

inferences.statement: The hosted API is Python FastAPI with Pydantic models (422 bodies shaped {detail:[{loc,msg,type}]}, unknown fields rejected), Postgres 16 as the system of record, Redis for cache/arq jobs, RabbitMQ for the call queue, S3 for recordings.
evidence: AGENTS.md SIP trunks rule 9 (error body shapes)

pre_registered_scoring_rule: Verifier marks each row TRUE / PARTLY / FALSE / NOT-CHECKABLE against the OSS repo at the HEAD commit on the day of checking (record the SHA). Hit rate = (TRUE + 0.5 PARTLY) / (TRUE + PARTLY + FALSE) over rows with checkable_in_oss=true and contamination in {none, possible}; report the 'none'-only rate separately. Brier score over the same rows using 'confidence'.
